name: Twyfelfontein or /Ui-//aes
description: In the dry sandstone hills of Namibia's Kunene Region, Twyfelfontein (also called ǀUi-ǁAis, "jumping waterhole") holds one of Africa's largest collections of rock engravings. Over 2,500 carvings of rhinos, elephants, ostriches, giraffes and animal footprints cover the slabs near a small spring. Hunter-gatherers and later herders used the place for rituals, and a few red ochre paintings survive in rock shelters.
